system.name: MoCE
system.one_liner: a framework that mixes context-aware diagnostic experts via a policy layer, control plane, and execution plane to find incident root causes

components.name: Policy layer
components.role: decides how to combine experts, which experts to run, and how much historical data to analyze

components.name: Library of Experts
components.role: collection of pre-built context-aware expert DAGs that the policy layer selects from

components.name: Control plane
components.role: creates a LazyDAG instance for the analysis based on the policies, running experts over telemetry to produce root causes

components.name: Execution plane
components.role: schedules all database and compute operations of the resulting MoCE DAG

components.name: Anomaly
components.role: the input anomaly incident specification that triggers the analysis

components.name: Telemetry 1
components.role: one telemetry source fed into an expert in the LazyDAG

components.name: Telemetry 2
components.role: another telemetry source fed into an expert in the LazyDAG

components.name: MoCE DAG
components.role: the concrete DAG of database and compute operations scheduled by the execution plane

content.key_idea: MoCE diagnoses incidents in four layers: a policy layer chooses experts and history length, a library supplies expert DAGs, a control plane runs a LazyDAG over telemetry to get root causes, and an execution plane schedules the resulting operations.
content.reading_order: Top-down: Policy layer and Library of Experts side by side, then through a dashed divider into the Control plane's DAG, then into the Execution plane below.

palette.used_for: dark cyan/blue structural lines of the Library of Experts diagrams
light cyan triangle icons for telemetry/anomaly inputs
burnt-orange fill of the RC/merge boxes in the Control plane's DAG

style.stroke: thin (~0.45pt) strokes, dashed horizontal rules separating the four layers
style.font: Gill Sans-like sans, 3.5-9.5pt, no bold weight, larger sizes for section titles
style.arrows: many small straight arrows with filled heads inside the DAG diagrams, plus larger connecting arrows between layers

encoding.color_means: dark blue/cyan = structural elements of the expert DAGs, green diamonds = expert computation nodes, orange = merged root-cause/RC output boxes, light-blue triangles = telemetry/anomaly inputs
encoding.line_style_means: dashed horizontal rules separate the four logical layers (policy, library, control, execution); solid arrows show data flow within and between layers
encoding.emphasis: the four layers are stacked and visually separated by dashed rules and bold section titles, mirroring the caption's explicit (a)-(d) component list; the Control plane's internal DAG reuses the Library of Experts' icon style to show it instantiates one of those expert graphs
reusable_patterns: stacked layered system diagram with an explicit small-multiples panel for a component that has many instances
database/pipeline icon row for the execution/scheduling layer
weaknesses: the internal DAG node labels in the Control plane are set in very small text that is hard to read even in the source figure
no explicit legend for the triangle vs. diamond icon shapes

evidence: MoCE is organized across four logical layers as shown in Figure 3
the DAG framework to author new context-aware experts (for the library of experts)
the mixture policy for routing incidents and combining results from experts

summary: Figure 3 shows the top-level architecture of MoCE, a root-cause diagnosis framework for Internet-scale services, organized into four logical layers. A Policy layer (top-left) decides how to combine experts, which experts to run, and how much historical data to analyze, drawing on a Library of Experts (top-right, shown as a small-multiples grid of expert DAGs). Below a dashed divider, the Control plane creates a LazyDAG instance from an anomaly specification and telemetry inputs, running expert computations (green diamond nodes) that merge into root causes. A second divider leads to the Execution plane, which schedules the resulting MoCE DAG's database and compute operations, shown as a row of pipeline/database icons. The figure is a compact, icon-heavy stacked-layer diagram using dark blue, green, and orange flat fills with no numbered steps.

notes: inner DAG node labels in the Control plane (the small RC.. boxes and the merge box) are too small to read reliably from the preview, so they are omitted as named components.
